sections.name: textFragments
sections.title: Cutting long text safely
sections.what: Splits text into pieces no longer than a limit, preferring to break at a space or new line, and never splitting an emoji or other two-part symbol.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: every character must survive a page break.
sections.watch_out: A break at a space is used only when it falls in the second half of the limit, otherwise the text is cut at the limit.

sections.name: paginateClaims
sections.title: Filling pages with claims
sections.what: Goes through the claims in order and fills each page until a size budget (default 900 characters) or item count (default 5) is reached, then starts a new page. Long claims continue onto following pages.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps each slide short enough to read.
sections.watch_out: Callers that rely on the defaults will all get the same page size, so changing the default affects every caller.

summary: Splits long text and groups claims into pages so no text is lost and no page is too full.
purpose: Lets long claim lists flow onto several slides without dropping or breaking any words.
why: Stated in the comment: preserve every character, including spaces and emoji, across page boundaries.
how: First, textFragments cuts a piece of text into chunks no longer than a limit, preferring to break at a space or new line, and never splits an emoji. Then paginateClaims goes through the claims in order, filling a page until it reaches a size budget of 900 characters or five items. When a claim does not fit, it is cut into fragments and continued on the next page.
inputs: A list of claims, each with text and an id. Optional budget and item limits, with defaults of 900 and 5.
outputs: A list of pages, each a list of claim pieces with the same ids and the text for that page.
risks: Default numbers are fixed, so any caller that relies on them gets the same page size. Very small limits throw an error. Text containing only long words with no spaces is cut at the limit.
debug: If text goes missing, compare the joined pages with the original claims, then check the fragment cut logic in textFragments. If pages overflow, check the budget values passed in. The matching test is in contentPagination.test.ts.
